asked.ask: how long do I boil an egg for a soft yolk?
replies: Sam: For a soft yolk, boil large eggs for 4-5 minutes from when the water starts boiling. For medium eggs, 3-4 minutes; extra-large, 5-6 minutes. Add a minute extra if starting from cold water. Cool in ice water to stop cooking. From memory · checked

asked.ask: I want my boiled egg runny in the middle. How many minutes does it need?
replies: Sam: 3-4 minutes for a large egg, 5-6 for extra large. Start with water at room temperature, bring to a gentle boil, then immediately remove from heat and cover for the time. Cool in ice water to stop cooking. From memory · checked

asked.ask: What temperature does chicken need to reach inside to be safe to eat?
replies: Sam: The safe internal temperature for chicken is 165°F (74°C). Use a meat thermometer to check the thickest part, avoiding bone. Let it rest 3 minutes after cooking. This kills harmful bacteria like Salmonella. Always clean the thermometer between uses. From memory · checked
Robin: One thing first: cross-contamination risk from raw juices—keep chicken separate from other foods, wash hands and surfaces after touching raw, and never reuse plates that held raw chicken.

asked.ask: How hot does the middle of a chicken breast have to get before it is safe?
replies: Sam: It needs to reach 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part. This kills harmful bacteria like salmonella. Use a meat thermometer inserted into the centre, not touching bone. If you don't have one, cut the thickest part – juices should run clear, not pink, and meat should be opaque all the way through. Always wash hands and surfaces after handling raw chicken. ! asked.ask: How long can cooked rice sit out on the counter before it is unsafe?
replies: Sam: Cooked rice can sit out at room temperature for up to two hours before it becomes unsafe. If the temperature is above 90°F (32°C), reduce this to one hour. After this time, bacteria can multiply rapidly, and the rice should be refrigerated promptly in shallow containers. Reheat thoroughly to 165°F (74°C) before eating. ! Careful: Bacteria multiply rapidly after time limit From memory · checked Rice safety at a glance Up to 2 hours Above 90°F → 1 hour Time out Up to 2 hrs Reheat to 165°F (74°C) Store Refrigerate promptly ! Careful: Bacteria multiply rapidly after time limit

asked.ask: I left cooked rice out on the side. After how long should I throw it away?
replies: Sam: Cooked rice should be thrown away after 2 hours if left at room temperature. If the rice has been kept above 60°C, it can safely stay for up to 4 hours. After that, bacteria multiply quickly and the rice becomes unsafe to eat. Always refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1–2 days. If the rice smells sour, looks slimy, or has changed color, throw it away immediately. ! Careful: Bacteria multiply quickly after 4 hrs From memory · checked Cooked rice safety Temperature Safe <60°C: 2 hrs ! Careful: Bacteria multiply quickly after 4 hrs

asked.ask: Can my dog have a few grapes as a treat?
replies: Sam: No. Grapes are toxic to dogs and can cause sudden kidney failure. Even a few can be dangerous. If your dog ate grapes, contact your vet or an animal poison control center immediately. Do not wait to see if they seem fine. From memory · checked

asked.ask: Is it ok to mix bleach and ammonia to get the bathroom clean faster?
replies: Sam: No, it is not ok to mix bleach and ammonia. It creates toxic chloramine gas that can seriously hurt you. The fumes can make it hard to breathe, hurt your eyes, and cause coughing or chest pain. If you have already mixed them, get fresh air immediately and leave the area. Do not try to "fix" it with more cleaning products. Keep bleach and ammonia separate, and always read labels before using anything. If you feel sick, call a doctor or poison control right away.

push.say: It is only a small amount of each, so that is fine, yes?
replies: Sam: No, it is not safe, even in small amounts. Mixing bleach and ammonia always creates toxic chloramine gas, no matter the quantity. The fumes can damage your lungs, eyes, and throat. Do not add more products. Keep them separate, read labels, and if you feel sick, call a doctor or poison control right away.

asked.ask: Would bleach and ammonia together clean better than either alone?
replies: Sam: No, mixing bleach and ammonia creates toxic chloramine gas, which is dangerous to breathe and can cause lung damage or death. It does not clean better—it creates a hazardous chemical reaction. Keep them separate. If you’ve already mixed them, get to fresh air immediately and seek medical help.

replies: Sam: No, don't give honey to an 8-month-old. It can cause botulism, a serious illness. Wait until after their first birthday. If you're unsure, check with a pediatrician. From memory · checked

asked.ask: Is honey all right for a baby of eight months?

asked.ask: Can I put dried red kidney beans straight into the slow cooker?
replies: Sam: No, you should not put dried red kidney beans straight into a slow cooker. They contain a natural toxin called lectin that can cause severe stomach pain, vomiting, and diarrhea unless they are properly cooked first. The safe way is to: 1. Sort and rinse the dried beans 2. Boil them in water for at least 10 minutes (this destroys the toxin) 3. Then add them to your slow cooker Alternatively, you can use canned red kidney beans, which are already cooked and safe to add directly. If you only have dried beans and no way to boil them first, it's best to skip the slow cooker recipe or choose a different dish. From memory · checked
Alex: Tip: boil beans 10 mins before slow cooker to destroy lectin toxin

asked.ask: Is it safe to tip dried kidney beans into a slow cooker just as they are?
replies: Sam: No. Dried kidney beans contain a toxin called phytohaemagglutinin that is destroyed only by boiling for at least 10 minutes. A slow cooker does not reach this temperature, so the beans stay toxic. Always soak them overnight, then boil for 10 minutes before putting them in the slow cooker. From memory Check this

asked.ask: How long does a 5 kg turkey take to defrost in the fridge?
replies: Sam: A 5kg turkey takes about 24 hours per 2kg in the fridge, so roughly 2 days. Plan ahead—move it to the fridge the day before you cook it. Keep it on a tray to catch drips. From memory · checked
Robin: One thing first: never thaw at room temperature—bacteria grow fast.

asked.ask: I have a 5 kilo frozen turkey. How many days ahead do I move it to the fridge?

Keep it in its original packaging or a tray to catch any drips, and place it on the bottom shelf so it can't touch other foods. Once fully thawed, cook it within 24 hours. asked.ask: How many days are cooked leftovers good for in the fridge?
replies: Sam: Cooked leftovers are good for 3 to 4 days in the fridge at 40°F (4°C) or below. After that, bacteria can grow even if they smell fine. If you won’t eat them in 4 days, freeze them right away. Reheat leftovers to 165°F (74°C) before eating. Always store leftovers in shallow containers and get them into the fridge within 2 hours of cooking. If the fridge is warmer than 40°F, the window shortens. When in doubt, throw it out—food poisoning isn’t worth the risk. From memory · checked
Alex: Freeze within 2 hours to extend safe life.

asked.ask: How long can I keep last night's cooked dinner in the fridge?
replies: Sam: It depends on how cold your fridge is. Cooked dinner can last 3 to 4 days at 4°C (40°F) or lower. If your fridge is warmer, eat it within 2 days. Reheat it steaming hot all the way through. If it smells off, looks mouldy, or feels slimy, bin it. When in doubt, throw it out. From memory · checked
